{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "Prompt: Build a clean, simple, fully responsive static landing page in Astro for an online photography course called "FrameCraft Studio". The visual direction should feel like Notion meets Material Design: lots of white space, soft gray page background, crisp cards, subtle shadows, rounded corners, organized content blocks, simple icons, calm typography, and a very structured layout. This is a static marketing page only, so use mock/sample course content, placeholder images, and local/static data. No login, no payment flow, no backend, no API, no database, no dashboard functionality.

Goal:
Create a polished landing page that convinces beginners and hobby photographers to enroll in a photography fundamentals course. It should feel trustworthy, modern, educational, and easy to scan. Keep the complexity simple but make the design look premium and complete.

Tech Requirements:
- Use Astro.
- Static front-end only.
- Use plain CSS or scoped Astro styles; no backend services.
- The page should render fully with static/sample content.
- Responsive design for mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Use semantic HTML sections.
- Smooth hover states and small tasteful transitions are welcome.

Design Style:
- Inspired by Notion layout clarity: clean blocks, document-like sections, tidy spacing.
- Material design influence: elevated cards, clear hierarchy, soft surfaces, contained buttons.
- Color palette: warm white, light stone gray, charcoal text, muted black, soft amber accent, and a small amount of camera-lens blue.
- Typography should be modern and readable, with strong headings and comfortable body text.
- Use simple line icons or emoji-style placeholders if needed, but keep it refined.
- Avoid heavy gradients; use very subtle background shapes or soft highlight panels.

Page Structure:

1. Top Navigation
- Left: FrameCraft Studio logo text with a small camera icon mark.
- Center/right nav links: Course, Curriculum, Projects, Reviews, FAQ.
- CTA button: "Join the Course".
- Sticky or visually persistent header preferred, but keep it simple.
- Mobile layout should collapse gracefully, even if it is just a stacked compact nav.

2. Hero Section
Headline:
"Learn Photography Like a Visual Notebook"

Subheadline:
"A calm, practical online course for beginners who want to understand light, composition, camera settings, and storytelling without feeling overwhelmed."

Primary CTA:
"Start Learning"

Secondary CTA:
"View Curriculum"

Hero visual idea:
Create a Notion-style learning dashboard card using static UI mockups, not real functionality. Include cards like:
- Module 01: Camera Basics
- Weekly Project: Golden Hour Portraits
- Progress: 6 Lessons
- Tip: Shoot in manual mode for 15 minutes daily

Add a small trust row under the hero:
- 2,400+ students
- 18 short lessons
- 6 guided projects
- Lifetime access

3. Course Snapshot Section
Title: "Everything you need to start shooting with confidence"
Use 3 or 4 Material-style cards:
- Camera Settings Made Simple: ISO, shutter speed, aperture explained visually.
- Composition Frameworks: rule of thirds, leading lines, balance, and negative space.
- Natural Light Practice: learn window light, golden hour, shadows, and contrast.
- Editing Basics: simple color correction workflow using sample images.

Each card should have a small icon, title, short description, and subtle hover elevation.

4. Curriculum Section
Make this look like a Notion document outline or course syllabus table. Use static accordion-looking blocks but they do not need to function unless easy with CSS only. Include:
Module 1: Camera Foundations
- Understanding exposure
- Auto vs manual mode
- Lens basics

Module 2: Light & Mood
- Soft light vs hard light
- Golden hour practice
- Indoor window portraits

Module 3: Composition
- Framing subjects
- Visual rhythm
- Storytelling through angles

Module 4: Editing Workflow
- Selecting your best photos
- Basic color correction
- Creating a consistent visual style

5. Featured Student Projects
Section title: "Practice with real creative assignments"
Use 3 project cards with placeholder image panels:
- The Morning Light Study
- Street Details Photo Walk
- One Subject, Ten Angles

Each card should include a tiny label like "Beginner Friendly", "30 min", or "Creative Challenge". Use static placeholder imagery or CSS image blocks with gradients that feel photography-related. No external image API required.

6. Instructor Section
Create a simple instructor bio block:
Name: Lena Hart
Role: Documentary Photographer & Visual Educator
Bio: "Lena teaches photography with a calm, systems-based approach, helping students move from random snapshots to intentional images."
Include a quote card:
"The goal is not expensive gear. The goal is learning to see."
Use a clean profile placeholder image/card.

7. Learning Experience Section
Show a two-column layout:
Left: Text explaining how the course works.
Right: A checklist card.
Checklist items:
- Watch short lessons at your own pace
- Complete weekly photo prompts
- Compare before and after examples
- Build a mini portfolio by the end
- Download static practice notes

Make it clear that this is a self-paced online course landing page, not a live app.

8. Testimonials Section
Use 3 static testimonials:
- Maya R. — "I finally understand manual mode without panic."
- Daniel K. — "The assignments made me look at ordinary places differently."
- Priya S. — "The course feels organized, simple, and beautifully paced."

Cards should match Material design with star ratings or small accent chips.

9. Pricing / Enrollment Section
Create a simple pricing card, not connected to payment:
Course Access
$79 one-time
Includes:
- 18 video lessons
- 6 guided projects
- Downloadable practice notes
- Beginner editing checklist
- Lifetime access to static course materials
CTA: "Join the Course"
Add small text: "Static demo button — no checkout integration required."

10. FAQ Section
Use clean Notion-style Q&A blocks:
- Do I need a professional camera?
Answer: No, a phone or beginner camera is enough.
- Is this course live?
Answer: No, it is designed as a self-paced online course.
- Are the projects beginner friendly?
Answer: Yes, every project uses everyday locations and natural light.
- Is there any account system?
Answer: No, this landing page is static and uses sample content only.

11. Final CTA Section
Headline: "Start seeing light, shape, and story everywhere."
Short text: "FrameCraft Studio gives you a simple path from snapshots to intentional photography."
Button: "Begin the Course"

12. Footer
Include:
- FrameCraft Studio
- Short tagline
- Links: Course, Curriculum, Projects, FAQ
- Copyright text for 2026

Responsiveness:
- Desktop: generous spacing, multi-column card grids, strong hero layout.
- Tablet: balanced two-column sections.
- Mobile: stacked sections, readable type, full-width buttons/cards.

Important Constraints:
- Static site only.
- Do not add authentication, backend routes, API calls, payments, database, or real course platform features.
- Mock data and placeholder images are fine.
- No 3D, WebGL, canvas game, or complex interactive mechanics.
- Keep it simple, elegant, and production-looking as a static Astro landing page.",
 "judge": {
  "model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8",
  "model_sha": "94125d2bd83076b21eed33119525e29eaf3894f4",
  "request_model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8:novita",
  "provider": "novita",
  "pinned_on": "2026-10-09",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "rubric_id": "rva1:mean(visual,query,asset)"
 }
}

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
